claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a lower-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K and approximately 30% strain.
Single-phase high-entropy alloys can have insufficient strength at elevated temperatures.
Approximately 1 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles will be introduced during mechanical alloying and consolidation.
The selected processing route will produce an even, nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion within the BCC matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as stable pinning centers for dislocations.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries.
The oxide dispersion will suppress dislocation motion at high temperature.
The oxide dispersion will retard high-temperature creep.
The oxide dispersion will limit grain coarsening at high temperature.
Particle-mediated suppression of dislocation motion and grain coarsening will maintain the alloy's strength at 1273 K.
The Y2O3-containing alloy will gain approximately 150–200 MPa in yield strength at 1273 K relative to the 330 MPa baseline.
The Y2O3-containing alloy will exceed approximately 500 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
The strengthened alloy will retain approximately 30% strain capacity at 1273 K.
Testing at 1273 K under tensile and compressive loading to approximately 30% strain represents the relevant W–TiVNbTa–CuCrZr intermediate-layer service conditions.
The magnitude of strengthening will depend on the uniformity and thermal stability of the Y2O3 dispersion and on processing parameters.

contradictions.description: An increase of 150 MPa over the stated 330 MPa baseline gives about 480 MPa, so the lower end of the predicted 150–200 MPa increase does not exceed the separately stated approximately 500 MPa target.
